chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), that it was said to him:

What is the reason that the believer is the most resolute of people? He (peace be upon him) said: Because the glory of the Quran is in his heart and the purity of faith is in his chest, and he worships Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, obedient to Allah and to His Messenger (peace be upon him), additional and confirming. It was said: What is the reason that the believer can be the most stingy of people? He said: Because he earns his livelihood from what is lawful, and seeking the lawful is difficult, so he does not like to part with it due to the hardship he knows is in seeking it. And if his soul is generous, he does not spend it except in its proper place.

It was said: What are the signs of the believer? He said: Four: his sleep is like the sleep of the drowned, his eating is like the eating of the sick, his weeping is like the weeping of the bereaved mother, and his sitting is like the sitting of the one against whom people are rallied.

It was said to him: What is the reason that the believer can be the most importunate in marriage? He said: Because he guards his private part from the private parts of what is not lawful for him, and so that his desire does not lead him astray this way and that way. And when he attains the lawful, he is content with it and makes himself independent of others through it.

And he (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, in the believer are three characteristics that are not found together except in him: his knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, his knowledge of whom he loves, and his knowledge of whom he hates.
And he said: Indeed, the strength of the believer is in his heart. Do you not see that you find him weak in body, thin in frame, yet he stands in prayer at night and fasts during the day?

And he said: The believer in his religion is firmer than the unshakable mountains. And that is because the mountain can be carved from, but no one can carve anything from the believer's religion. And that is due to his frugality with his religion and his stinginess for it.
ai.seo_question: What are the distinctive ethical and spiritual signs of a true believer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Attributed to Imam al-Sadiq in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Sifat al-Shia*, this hadith elucidates the paradoxical nature of the believer, reconciling apparent contradictions like resoluteness and frugality through the lens of spiritual discipline and the high cost of seeking lawful sustenance. It further defines the believer’s physical demeanor—such as sleep resembling that of the drowning and sitting like the leaper—as outward manifestations of inner devotion, while emphasizing that their true strength lies in the heart’s steadfastness against external erosion of faith.

en.badr-shahin: My father, Allah may have mercy upon him, narrated to us from Abdullah bin Ja’far al-Himyari from Harun bin Muslim from Mas’ada bin Sadaqa:

As he was asked about the clear resoluteness that is seen in the manners of the believers, Abu Abdullah (a) answered: This is because of the existence of the glory of the Quran in the believers’ hearts and the existence of the purity of faith in their chests. They worship Allah, Powerful and Majestic is He, obey Him, and believe the Messenger of Allah. They asked: What about the stinginess that is noticed in the believers’ manners? He (a) answered: This is because the believers seek only legal earnings. To seek legal earnings is something very hard; therefore, the believers dislike to forsake the things that they exerted all efforts painstakingly to obtain. When they are generous, they spend so properly.

They asked: What are the characters of the believers? He (a) answered: The believers sleep like the drowned, eat like the ailed, weep like the mother that is bereaved of her child, and sit like the one against whom people are rallied.

They asked: Why are the believers more importunate than others are in the question of marriage? He (a) answered: This is because the believers restrain their carnal desires and do not violate the others’ honors. Besides, they do so in order that their sexual drives will not lead them astray. If a believer gains the legal, he satisfies himself with it and dispends with anything else.
• Imam as-Sadiq (a) also said: Only the believers enjoy three characters altogether: the knowledge of Allah, knowledge of those whom they like, and knowledge of those whom they dislike.
• He (a) also said: A believer’s power lies in his heart; therefore, he stays up at nights (for worship) and observes fasting during days while his body is weak and thin.

• He (a) also said: With regard to his religion, the believer is firmer than the unshakable mountains. One can take from the unshakable mountains, while no one can take anything from the beliefs of the believers, for they are so observant and abiding by his religion.
